messages:
maya: Heads up — saw a sharp jump in NVMe SMART err_count and write-amplification on the scratch pool right after the kernel roll (2026-03-17). Eviction rate for ephemeral volumes is ~4x normal and GPU provisioning backlog jumped (~120 pending pods). fs metrics + small logs below. :warning:

maya: ```
metric: scratch_evictions_per_min  -> 12 -> 48
metric: nvme_err_count(nvme0)       -> 12 -> 412
metric: device_write_amp(nvme0)     -> 1.2 -> 3.9
logs: kernel: nvme_core: error_count incremented for nvme0 
```

omar: Which regions/nodes are affected? Any correlation to specific firmware?

maya: Primary hit is eu-west2 (gnode-evict-33x) and a handful in us-west2 (gnode-210..215). I cross-referenced firmware and most are on FW 2.1.7; baseline healthy ones are mixed 2.1.5/2.1.6. Correlation looks stronger with kernel 6.4.8 -> 6.5.1 roll we pushed.

sre-bot: ALERT: nvme_err_count surge on cluster=redwood-prod-eu-west2, severity=high, triggered at 2359876500

dina: Immediate mitigation suggestions: ramp down ephemeral-cleaner concurrency and suspend aggressive TRIM/GC during peak. We should also stop new batch placements to affected nodes. Example ops commands: 

```
opsctl cleaner update --concurrency 10 --trim-window "02:00-05:00"
kubectl label nodes gnode-evict-33{1..6} scratch_issue=true
```

I'll push the cleaner change now.

tj: Also recommend tagging + cordon + drain the worst nodes from GPU scheduler before we get more job failures: 

```
kubectl label node gnode-evict-331 no-schedule=scratch-issue
kubectl cordon gnode-evict-331
kubectl drain gnode-evict-331 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

omar: If this is firmware-related we have options: firmware patch roll (vendor) vs wholesale replacements vs rebalancing workloads to more durable SKUs. Quick back-of-envelope: 120 suspect drives * $400 = $48k one-time replacement. Rebalancing to premium NVMe adds ~$0.06/hr/node -> ~$4k/mo at current fleet size. Hardware replacement has CapEx hit but lower ops risk.

maya: Doing the cordon/drain now for the worst 4 nodes (gnode-evict-331..334). Cleaner concurrency update applied to 10.

dina: I've opened vendor ticket (REF-7842) and included SMART dumps + kernel oops. Asked for firmware sampling on 10 drives; vendor requested we hold on mass firmware rollout until samples returned.

tj: I'll take node ownership and routing changes — will update the maintenance board and set a temporary policy to avoid scheduling batch jobs on nodes labeled `scratch_issue=true`.

omar: I'll prepare replacement procurement options and a quick spreadsheet comparing: immediate replacements vs 3-month rebalancing vs conservative rollback to kernel 6.4.8. Rough cost + ops impact by EOD.

maya: Plan for now: 1) throttle cleaner (done), 2) cordon/drain worst nodes (in progress), 3) hold kernel mass roll for other regions, 4) vendor sampling + firmware decision in 48-72h.

maya: Action owners -> dina: vendor follow-up + sample results; tj: node drains + scheduler policy; omar: cost options; maya: monitoring + rollback plan. Will ping here with periodic status. :thumbsup:
